newsitem.title: QATAR: Qatar shares extend upbeat trend.
newsitem.headline: Qatar shares extend upbeat trend.

text.p: Shares on Qatar's unofficial stock market extended their surge during the week to Thursday with investors expecting strong year-end gains, brokers said.

"We end the year on a cheerful note with the index again up and the coming year expected to bring some exciting developments," said Mazin al-Shakarchi, senior treasury and investment manager at the Commercial Bank of Qatar (CBQ).
An official Doha Securities Market will start functioning in the second quarter of 1997 and the market may be opened to Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) citizens, he said.
During the week to Thursday, 10 shares rose and seven were steady, pushing the CBQ's 18-share index up to 126.32 points from 125.41 in the previous week.
Only Qatar Insurance shares declined, shedding 10 riyals to 650, amid rumours of lower-than-expected profit at the year-end.
The market leader, Qatar National Bank, rose 10 riyals to 630. The heavyweight Qatar Navigation and Qatar General Insurance also rose 10 riyals each to 780 and 575 respectively.
Doha Bank Ltd and the CBQ advanced two riyals to 285 and 352 and Al Ahli Bank of Qatar one riyal to 223.
Qatar Cement and Qatar Cinema also gained two riyals each to 315 and 185 and Qatar Flour Mills and Qatar Real Estate Company closed one riyal higher each at 311 and 53 respectively.
